children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar ahead of U.S. CPI data due later today. This data "could influence market pricing for the timing of the Fed's next [rate] increase," CBA's Carol Kong says in a research report. "The risk is the core CPI surprises to the upside because of strong consumer demand and higher costs, pushing up market pricing of an October Fed hike and the USD," the economist and currency strategist adds. The U.S. dollar edges 0.1% higher to 158.38 yen, but is 0.1% lower at 1,339.20 won, while the Australian dollar is up 0.1% at US$0.6988, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
